candidates.change_summary: Change `block.number + 1` to `block.number` in the assignment to `guesses[msg.sender].block`.
Change `block.number + 1` to `block.number + 2` in the assignment to `guesses[msg.sender].block`.
Delete the `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` statement.
Remove the `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` check.
Replace the require checking that the sender has no existing guess with a require that is always true, so lockInGuess can be called repeatedly.
Delete the require checking that the sender has no existing guess, so lockInGuess can be called repeatedly.
Change the payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to at least 1 ether, so lockInGuess accepts larger payments.
Change the payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to at most 1 ether, so lockInGuess accepts smaller payments.
Set the stored block number to the current block instead of the next block, changing the lock-in timing.
Set the stored block number to block.number + 2 instead of block.number + 1, changing the lock-in timing.
Store the hash parameter into the block field instead of the guess field, corrupting the observable recorded guess.
Do not store the provided hash, leaving the guess field unchanged for the sender.
Remove the requirement that the caller has not already locked in a guess, allowing lockInGuess to overwrite an existing guess.
Remove the requirement that exactly 1 ether is sent, allowing lockInGuess to succeed with any msg.value.
Change the required payment from exactly 1 ether to exactly 2 ether.
Change the stored guess from the provided hash to a fixed constant value.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Swap the order of the two statements so the block is updated before the guess is stored.
Reset the caller's guess block back to 0 immediately after storing the new guess and block.
Replace the initial guess-lock guard so it checks the guess value instead of the block number.
Replace the required payment amount from 1 ether to 2 ether.
Change the stored block number to the current block number instead of the next block number.
Change the stored block number to one block earlier than the intended next block.
Delete the require that enforces exactly 1 ether is sent.
Delete the assignment that stores the guess hash.
Delete the assignment that stores the target block number.
Delete the require that the caller has not already locked in a guess, allowing repeated lockInGuess calls to overwrite the stored block number and guess.
Change the payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to exactly 2 ether, so lockInGuess no longer completes under the original valid call conditions.
Store the supplied hash into the block field instead of the guess field, changing which stored value is observable after lockInGuess completes.
Store the current block number directly instead of block.number + 1, changing the stored block value after lockInGuess completes.
Store block.number - 1 instead of block.number + 1 in the stored block field, changing the stored block value after lockInGuess completes.
Change the overwrite guard to require the stored block to already be nonzero, so lockInGuess reverts on a first call instead of completing.
Drop the `.block` field access in the overwrite guard, so the check reads the whole Guess struct incorrectly and changes when lockInGuess completes.
Changed the block stored in the Guess struct from block.number + 1 to 0, which makes future lockInGuess calls by the same sender still require the initial block==0 and thus allows repeated guessing.
Changed the guessed hash assignment to store a fixed zero hash instead of the provided hash parameter.
Changed the initial guess-block guard to require a nonzero block, inverting when lockInGuess can be called.
Changed the ETH value guard from exactly 1 ether to at most 1 ether, allowing calls with less than 1 ether.
Deleted the require that enforces the caller has not already locked in a guess.
Deleted the require that enforces exactly 1 ether is sent, allowing calls with any msg.value.
Remove the one-time lock check requiring guesses[msg.sender].block == 0, allowing repeated lock-in calls before settling.
Remove the 1 ether payment requirement, allowing lock-in without sending ether.
Set the stored guess block to the current block number instead of block.number + 1, changing when settle() can be called.
Do not store the provided hash as the guess, leaving guesses[msg.sender].guess unset while still marking the block.
Move the guess assignment after the block assignment; this is semantically equivalent and should be considered only if reordering the two state writes is treated as an allowed move.
Replace the first require condition inside lockInGuess with a tautology, removing the one-guess-per-address restriction.
Delete the require that enforces msg.value == 1 ether in lockInGuess.
Change the stored target block height from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the stored target block height to block.number + 2.
Delete the statement that stores the guess hash in lockInGuess.
Delete the statement that updates the guess block number in lockInGuess.
Change the mapping key used when storing the guess hash from msg.sender to address(this).
Change the lockInGuess guess assignment to store the hash in the block field instead of the guess field, leaving the block field unchanged.
Change the stored guess hash to an unrelated mutated hash by XORing the input with 1.
Set the guess lock block to the current block instead of the next block, changing when settle can be called.
Remove the 1 ether msg.value requirement so lockInGuess can be called without payment.
Change the initial-guess guard to require an already nonzero guesses[msg.sender].block, preventing first-time lock-in.
Remove the line that stores the submitted hash, so the guess remains unchanged.
Remove the line that stores the lock block, so guesses[msg.sender].block remains zero and settle cannot be used.
Move the guess-hash assignment after the block assignment; both writes still execute on successful calls.
Replace the condition in the require to allow settling immediately instead of after the block number.
Change the answer computation to use a different block number (the current block instead of the guess block).
Remove the transfer, so the contract never pays out even on a correct guess.
Change the transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Delete the statement that resets guesses[msg.sender].block to 0, allowing repeated settle attempts.
Change the equality check to inequality, reversing the payout condition.
Replace blockhash with a different hash function that changes the answer.
Removed the line that resets guesses[msg.sender].block to zero before checking the guess.
Changed the payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Changed the blockhash input from guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number.
Changed the block-number require from strictly greater-than to greater-than-or-equal.
Changed the guess-comparison condition from equality to inequality.
Change the payout transfer amount in settle() from 2 ether to 0 ether.
Change the settlement guard to require block.number < guesses[msg.sender].block instead of >.
Change the answer hash to use blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block + 1) instead of blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block).
Change the answer hash to use keccak256(abi.encodePacked(blockhash(block.number - 1))) instead of the stored block's hash.
Remove the equality comparison so the payout condition checks guess != answer instead of guess == answer.
Remove the line that resets the caller's guesses block to zero before payout.
Replace the caller's block reset with a reset to the current block number instead of zero.
Change the payout condition to compare the stored guess against itself, making it always true when reached.
Change the payout condition to compare the answer against itself, making it always true when reached.
Change the initial block-zero guard to require guesses[msg.sender].block == 0 instead of != 0.
Change the stored answer hash input to hash the caller's address instead of the previous blockhash.
Insert a second payout transfer of another 2 ether after the conditional transfer.
Change the payout transfer recipient from msg.sender to address(this).
Change the strict block-number check from `>` to `>=`, allowing settlement in the same block as lockInGuess's target block.
Use the current block's hash instead of the stored guess block hash when computing the answer.
Remove the blockhash call from the answer computation so the answer is just the hash of the guessed block number encoded.
Change the stored guess type assumption in the answer computation by hashing the raw guess value instead of the block hash.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the equality check so a wrong guess is paid instead of a correct guess.
Delete the requirement that the stored guess block is nonzero, allowing repeated settlement attempts without a prior lockInGuess.
Delete the requirement that the current block number is greater than the stored guess block, removing the time gate.
Delete the reset of the stored guess block to zero before payout, allowing replay settlement.
Delete the conditional payout entirely so settle never transfers ether.
Reset the stored guess block to the current block number instead of zero, changing post-settlement state and replay behavior.
Reset only the stored guess hash to zero while leaving the block number intact, changing post-settlement state.
Change the answer computation to use blockhash(block.number) instead of blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block).
Change the answer computation to hash only the blockhash without abi.encodePacked.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 0 ether.
Delete the requirement that the guess block has not yet passed.
Delete the requirement that the sender has an existing guess.
Delete the reset of the sender's guess block to zero after settling.
Delete the conditional payout so settle never transfers ether.
Insert an additional reset of the sender's guess block to zero before the payout check.
Move the reset of the sender's guess block to zero before computing the answer.
Replace the strict block-number progress guard with an inclusive comparison, allowing settlement in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Change the payout transfer target from the caller to this contract, preventing successful guessers from receiving the 2 ether payout.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering the observable balance change on a successful settlement.
Replace the equality check with an inequality check, so the payout occurs on an incorrect guess instead of a correct one.
Delete the successful-guess payout conditional, so no ether is ever transferred on settle.
Move the reset of the caller's guess block to after the payout check, so the guess is not cleared before determining and paying a winner.
Change the payout transfer from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Remove the block-number requirement that settlement can only occur after the guessed block.
Change the answer hash from blockhash to the current block number.
Change the answer hash from blockhash to the zero hash constant.
Change the equality check to an inequality check before paying out.
Delete the reset of the caller's block field before evaluating the payout condition.
Reset the stored guess hash instead of the block field.
Delete the payout transfer after a correct guess.
Delete the check that requires an existing guess-block before settling.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether in the successful-settle branch.
Change the comparison to always fail by comparing the guess against the zero hash instead of the computed answer.
Remove the block-number precondition so settle can be called before the target block is in the past.
Remove the initial guess-existence precondition so settle can be called without a prior lock-in.
Remove the reset of the caller's guess block to zero, leaving settlement state unchanged after a successful call.
Insert an additional guard requiring the guess to already equal the computed answer before resetting and paying out, making the payout path unreachable through the normal flow.
Change the settlement payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 0 ether.
Change the settlement winner condition to compare the stored guess against a keccak256 hash of itself rather than the blockhash-based answer.
Change the timing guard so settle requires the current block to be strictly less than the guessed block instead of greater.
Delete the guard that prevents settling before the guessed block has passed.
Delete the guard that requires an existing guess before settling.
Change the payout to always send 2 ether whenever settle is called after the timing guard, regardless of whether the guess was correct.
